contexts.text: (Why the Lord inquires of man what He already knows). AC 1931. AC 5800:end. AC 6132.
In the sense of the letter, this is an interrogation by the Lord; but, in the internal sense, it is the infinite perception of all things.
Let us ask her mouth () = ... to perceive whether she consents.
She went to ask Jehovah () = a state of communication. To ask, when said of the Lord, = to be communicated...
To ask () = to diligently inquire.
Jacob asked and said... (). AC 4296.

Interrogations in the sense of the letter are not interrogations in the supreme sense; for the Lord, who is treated of in that sense, has no need to interrogate man... Therefore this interrogation... = acknowledgement.
He asked the men of that place () = that truths were consulted. To ask = to consult.

The man in asking asked about us () = that he clearly perceived the things which were in the Natural. To ask = to perceive another's thought... because in Heaven there is a communication of all thoughts, insomuch that no one has need to ask another what he is thinking. AC 5800.
He asked them as to peace () = a perception that it is well. To ask = to perceive another's thoughts.
For in the internal sense an interrogation denotes Knowledge from perception.
It shall be that thy son shall ask thee () = perception from the truth which is of conscience. (For) to ask = Knowledge from perception.
They asked a man his companion as to peace () = a mutual Divine celestial state. Explained.

To interrogate Jehovah () = to be instructed concerning the truths and goods of the Church and of worship; for all interrogation of Jehovah is done for the sake of instruction concerning these things.
The less wise interrogate the more wise; and these the Lord...
To the inquiry about Abraham... they replied...
The will to interrogate. Signified.
The Angels said, Let us discourse by questions and answers, because the perception of a thing... does not remain, unless the hearer thinks about it from himself, and asks questions.
Luther... by turns permitted questions...
Ask and see ().
He who loves truth because it is truth, can as it were interrogate the Lord in doubtful things of faith, and receive answers from Him; but no where else than in the Word...
